answer: Each newcomer needs two established operators to cross-sign, and both signers lose part of their vested balance when the recruit turns out to be a clone. A rejected review goes to a fresh, unrelated panel instead of being cleared, so the fraud has to survive the same scrutiny twice. On the wharf that is the whole cost: a gale of new keys needs two thousand real signatures, and the payout is an opal still in the rock, vesting over future work.
